alerts.desc: Content Security Policy (CSP) adds a layer of security which helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks such as Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks.
alerts.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is properly configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header without wildcard directives.

alerts.desc: The 'unsafe-inline' allows the use of inline resources, such as inline <style> elements and style attributes.
alerts.solution: Ensure that your web server is properly configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header and avoid 'unsafe-inline'.

alerts.desc: X-Frame-Options header is not included in the HTTP response to protect against 'Clickjacking' attacks.
alerts.solution: Most modern Web browsers support the X-Frame-Options HTTP header. Ensure it is set on all web pages returned by your site.

alerts.desc: No Anti-CSRF tokens were found in a HTML submission form.
alerts.solution: Phase: Architecture and Design. Use a vetted library or framework that does not allow this weakness to occur.

alerts.alert: Incomplete or No Cache-control and Pragma HTTP Header Set
alerts.desc: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content.
alerts.solution: Whenever possible ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with 'no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate'.
